newsitem.title: INDIA: Major quake rocks central India, at least 27 dead.
newsitem.headline: Major quake rocks central India, at least 27 dead.

text.p: At least 27 people were killed and 150 injured when a major earthquake struck central India early on Thursday, toppling houses and burying many victims in their sleep, officials said.
"Twenty-seven people have died in the quake which hit Jabalpur town and nearby areas," Ajay Singh, a senior local official, told Reuters.
"The death toll may go up, but not substantially," he said, adding that rescue operations were underway. Unofficial reports said about 50 people had died.

A spokesman of the government of Madhya Pradesh state told Reuters the quake's epicentre was near Jabalpur city, about 260 km (160 miles) southeast of Bhopal. Most of the victims died when their houses collapsed on them, he said.
"When the earthquake struck, it was like the sound of machines in factories," Rajendra Bhatia, marketing manager for a pharmaceuticals firm in Jabalpur, said.

The tremor, which lasted about 50 seconds, struck at 4.22 a.m. (2252 GMT Wednesday) and measured 6.0 on the Richter scale, a state government spokeswoman in New Delhi said. Earthquakes of force six on the Richter scale can cause widespread damage.
"People are being taken in large numbers to hospital," the spokeswoman said. "According to our information many are still trapped under debris."
Buildings in Jabalpur were damaged by the quake, which officials said was preceded by a smaller tremor and was followed by an aftershock.

"At two government hospitals, Victoria and Medical College, there are masses of people along with rescue officials," Bhatia said. "Most of the people at the hospitals seem to be from villages close to Jabalpur."
Cracks appeared in the municipal corporation building in Jabalpur. A corner of the city's clock tower collapsed.

Bhatia said: "Windows were shattered. There are large cracks on small houses. Some homes have collapsed. People are afraid that there may be yet another earthquake and there are rumours to this effect. But business is normal and shops have opened."
Authorities said damage in the rural districts was more extensive and centred around Amandpur village, some 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Jabalpur.
The large Bargi dam on the Narmada River, the largest waterway in the landlocked state, was not affected by the quake, local officials told Reuters.
All India Radio said the "severe" quake damaged at least 500 houses.
In September 1993, some 10,000 people died in neighbouring Maharashtra state when a quake measuring 6.3 on the Richter scale struck the Latur-Osmanabad region.
